notes: Edited volume mostly focused on identity, religion, and frontier interaction. For an economics-focused chapter it is uneven, but it contains a few strong sections with explicit fiscal/tenurial content (ius colonatus and taxation obligations for settled prisoners-of-war) and an explicitly economic-integration chapter ('Barbarian Raiders and Barbarian Peasants') with a useful methodological warning about the limits of anecdotal written evidence for economic impact claims.
